doc.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Studio work versus jazz identity
summary: Creative jazz needs identity while commercial music asks you to sound like everyone else.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: How do you feel that the studio work was different from the big band playing?

Oh, well you know, this is a different ball game altogether, because when you’re playing creative music, jazz, you know your identity is important. But when you’re playing commercial music, you have to sacrifice your identity to sound like everybody else. So it’s a different thing altogether.

Have you noticed when Basie was recording did they ever, there were certain times when you might have done like there was a Broadway record I think that was done? How did he fit into the changing times?
I wasn’t there then. See I’ve been away from the band over 30 years. So by the time he started doing that I wasn’t around.
